title: The most in-demand skills for a UX Designer, according to recruiters
description: The five skills recruiters look for most in UX designers: empathy, prototyping, design systems, data and critical thinking.
updateNote: Revised in October 2026: I added what has changed since publication and a new visual to explain the core idea.

blocks.text: With the UX designer's role constantly evolving, it's essential to keep an eye on the trends and the skills recruiters value most. Today, beyond mastering design techniques, professionals need a set of hard and soft skills that position them as key players in building digital products.

Empathy is still one of the most crucial skills for UX designers. It involves the ability to put yourself in the user's shoes to understand their frustrations and desires. That deep understanding makes it possible to create user-centered solutions that actually solve problems. On top of that, effective communication skills are essential to articulate ideas, collaborate with cross-functional teams and negotiate with stakeholders. Collaborative thinking is increasingly in demand as design projects become more complex and more integrated with other areas of the business (CareerFoundry, 2023).

blocks.caption: The article's five skills, based on the sources cited at the end.

blocks.text: 2. Mastery of Prototyping and Wireframing Tools

Tools like Figma, Sketch and Adobe XD remain indispensable for creating interactive prototypes that allow usability testing before full development. Rapid prototyping, especially in agile work environments, has become one of the basic requirements for any UX designer. In addition, using collaborative design tools like Figma helps bring design and development teams together in real time (Adobe, 2023).

As more companies adopt design systems to ensure visual and functional consistency, mastering these component libraries has become a strategic skill. UX writing is also on the rise, with growing demand for designers who know how to write clear, objective copy, like error messages and usage instructions. This skill improves the user experience by making interfaces more accessible and intuitive (CareerFoundry, 2023).

Beyond creating design solutions, UX professionals need to know how to evaluate the impact of those solutions through metrics. Data analysis tools like Google Analytics and Hotjar help understand user behavior and continuously improve the experience based on concrete data. User research has also become a differentiator, with recruiters looking for designers who know how to plan and run interviews, A/B tests and quantitative and qualitative research (Adobe, 2023).
6. Knowing how to direct AI (2026 update)

Since the first version of this post, a new skill has joined the list: giving AI context, constraints and criteria, and evaluating what it delivers with a critical eye. It's not about memorizing prompts, it's about knowing what to ask for.
7. Understanding business and talking with code

With functional prototypes becoming more and more common, designers who understand business metrics and can talk with development are gaining ground. I write about this in “The Product Designer's new edge may be knowing how to talk with code.”

In a market that demands constant innovation, critical thinking is a valued skill, especially when it comes to questioning assumptions and proposing more effective solutions. Curiosity and a drive for continuous learning are also sought-after traits, since the UX field is constantly changing. Designers who stay up to date with new trends and keep improving their skills are the ones who stand out in hiring processes (CareerFoundry, 2023).
